SID’S MICROBIOME · RESEARCH & CONTEXT

What does Sid's microbiome data tell us about his immune state or response?

Why look at gut bacteria?

Some gut bacteria can influence the immune system. Researchers are studying whether they help explain responses to cancer immunotherapy. Sid’s documented treatment includes dostarlimab, which blocks PD-1 to release a brake on immune cells.

The studies below mostly involve other cancers. A species or strain studied in those experiments may differ from the bacteria measured here, and these stool profiles do not directly measure Sid’s immune activity.

THE DATA BEHIND THIS PAGE

Sid’s profiles and the comparison group

Sid · 5 stool profiles, 1 person

October 2025–March 2026, alongside documented treatment events. February has conflicting reported dates; March dates are receipt dates, with collection dates unavailable.

Five repeat observations of one person. Clinical response and direct immune measurements are not linked here.

Controls · 16 of the 96 UFPF profiles

These charts use the 16 control participants from the University of Florida cohort. The other profiles—53 Parkinson’s disease, 26 inflammatory bowel disease and 1 uncertain diagnosis—are excluded from this control comparison.

This small study group is not a representative sample of the healthy population. Full processing equivalence with Sid’s profiles is unverified.

Reading the charts: Percentages show each group’s share of the whole microbial profile retained for this comparison, after filtering and normalization. The denominator includes all retained groups, not only the bacteria shown in a chart. These are relative profile shares, not absolute bacterial counts. The dashed line is the middle value among the 16 controls; the grey band contains their middle 50%. These are reference values, not health targets or confidence intervals. * marks the conflicting February date; † marks March lab receipt dates.

Why include weight/metabolic medicines?

Wegovy (semaglutide) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) affect appetite and slow stomach emptying, so diet and digestion may be useful context to record. This does not show either caused the microbial changes. Wegovy label ↗ · Zepbound label ↗ · Metformin trial context ↗

SUPPORTING EVIDENCE & LIMITATIONS

Sources, interpretation and open questions

Data sources and chart provenance

The four genus charts and the Bacteroides species chart/table use the same prepared TSV reference-comparison profiles (16 Controls). The Bacteroides table shows species control medians; its two-species chart has no whole-genus reference band. Treatment dates come from sid-events.json.

Dates, baseline and clinical limits

The first observed sample was already during treatment, so it is a starting observation rather than an untreated baseline. February’s date has a public-metadata/lab-report conflict. March dates are lab receipt dates, with unavailable collection dates. One person and five repeated observations cannot establish cause, benefit, diagnosis, or a treatment recommendation.

A careful note on Akkermansia context

The model’s genus group contains the Atlas annotation Akkermansia sp KLE1798; equivalence to A. muciniphila is not established here. A defined A. muciniphila preparation studied in overweight, insulin-resistant adults is not evidence explaining this spike. Study record ↗
